item.title: Grid triples, link cobordisms in $\CPbar$ and the computation of Heegaard-Floer TQFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.03714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one. Individual sheets may wrap around the torus in the unblocked theory, whereas they are embedded in the blocked theory. In each fixed \(\SpinC\) structure, the map is determined by a finite enumeration. A difference number computed from the triangular regions determines the \(\SpinC\) structure of a Whitney triangle. Together with the topology of the associated surface, this gives an explicit formula for the absolute bigrading of each summand of the cobordism map. After basepoint reduction, the formula determines the Laurent monomial representing any nonzero map on the rank-one torsion-free two-variable knot Floer modules, yielding vanishing and ideal-containment criteria. We apply the construction to an affine family of grid links \(K(n;p,s)\), obtaining explicit cobordisms involving infinite families of torus knots and links, together with closed formulas for the bigradings of their distinguished grid states.
item.dc:creator: Roohallah Mahkam

item.title: Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions. For polyhedral products, we combine these results with their description by relative graph products and graph products of pairs. We also obtain bounds and exact computations for amenable category, together with applications to simplicial volume and Borel rigidity of closed aspherical polyhedral-product manifolds.
item.dc:creator: I. Gkeneralis, S. Prassidis

item.title: A surface-group action on real-hyperbolic space with no Cannon--Thurston map
item.description: arXiv:2611.03855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present discrete, faithful and purely loxodromic representations of a closed surface group of genus 431, and of a free group, into the group of isometries of a finite-dimensional real-hyperbolic space for which no Cannon--Thurston map exists. The construction combines three ingredients: the small-cancellation strategy employed by Baker--Riley to construct a subgroup of an ambient hyperbolic group with no Cannon--Thurston map, the realization of these groups by octagon complexes, and a theorem of Desgroseilliers--Haglund that supplies a convex cocompact faithful representation of the ambient hyperbolic group on a real-hyperbolic space. These examples admit ray Cannon--Thurston maps, as defined by Halder, Mahan Mj and Sardar.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Dular

item.title: Universal bounds for decompositions of PL manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.04095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The geometric dimension of a nonempty compact PL manifold $N$ is the smallest nonnegative integer $d$ for which $N$ admits a handle decomposition with all handles of index at most $d$. A PL filling of a compact PL manifold is a decomposition into compact codimension $0$ PL submanifolds, called sectors, with pairwise disjoint interiors and intersections described by standard local models. We advance Singhof's program of simplifying the sectors of a filling and their intersections. Specifically, for integers $m, \ell\ge 1$ and nonnegative integers $a_1\le\cdots\le a_\ell$, we prove that every closed PL $m$-manifold admits a filling into $\ell$ sectors whose nonempty $r$-fold intersections have geometric dimension at most $a_r$ for each $1\le r\le \ell$ if and only if \[ a_{\lambda_1}+\cdots+a_{\lambda_q}\ge m-\ell+1 \] for every partition $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_q=\ell$ into positive integers. Under the same inequalities, any prescribed $\ell$-sector filling of the boundary of a compact PL $m$-manifold extends to a filling with the corresponding relative handle index bounds. Necessity follows from the cup-product obstructions of Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. To prove sufficiency, we develop compatible handle trades that simplify intersections in increasing order of depth. For nondecreasing tuples of nonnegative integers, our theorem resolves the PL classification problem posed by Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. In particular, we obtain the bound $(2,2,4)$ for $3$-sector fillings in dimension $6$ and improve the $5$-sector bound $(1,2,3,3,4)$ of Rubinstein and Tillmann to $(1,2,2,3,4)$ in dimension $8$.
item.dc:creator: Rustam Sadykov

item.title: Smooth and Topological Nonorientable Four-Genera of Low-Crossing Knots
item.description: arXiv:2611.04243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare linking-form bounds with the smooth and locally flat nonorientable 4-genera of low-crossing knots. For every prime knot with at most 13 crossings whose Witt-level linking-form bound is at least 2, this bound equals both genera. We also exhibit 41 prime knots with 12 or 13 crossings that bound locally flat M\"obius bands but no smooth ones, and whose smooth nonorientable 4-genus is 2. Our methods combine linking forms, Heegaard Floer correction terms and definite-lattice obstructions with explicit band constructions. They determine 3,300 of the 3,525 values left unknown in KnotInfo on 2 November 2026; the remaining 225 knots have range $[1,2]$. We obtain new lower bounds of 2 for 2,102 knots with 14 crossings and correct previously reported values for three knots with 11 crossings.
item.dc:creator: Seong-Jin Lee

item.title: Exotic Dehn twists on sums of 4-manifolds, nuclei, and exotic structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.04541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For closed 4-manifolds $X_1, X_2$, we give a sufficient condition, in terms of the Seiberg-Witten invariants of $X_i$, for the Dehn twist on $X_1\#X_2$ along the neck to be smoothly nontrivial. This provides a broad generalization of the result of Kronheimer-Mrowka for $K3\#K3$. We also show that the boundary Dehn twists on the punctured connected sums of many pairs of elliptic surfaces are smoothly nontrivial. We also detect new examples of exotic Dehn twists along Seifert fibered 3-manifolds in elliptic surfaces. As a consequence, we exhibit a new phenomenon in which "exotic diffeomorphisms detect exotic smooth structures on 4-manifolds": the triviality of the boundary Dehn twist characterizes the standard nucleus $N(n)$ among the nuclei $N(n)_{p,q}$ homeomorphic to it, provided that $n\equiv0 \bmod 4$. These results are proved by computing the families Bauer-Furuta invariant for a new framing of the families Dirac index.
item.dc:creator: Hokuto Konno

item.title: Morse homology of nonsingular Morse-Smale foliations and its duality theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a Morse homology of the foliation which is defined by a general nonsingular Morse-Smale flow, applying the framework of the Conley index theory. In fact, we define a chain and a boundary homomorphism, therefore, a cochain and a cohomology are obtained as well. Furthermore, we prove a duality theorem on the homology and the cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Shigeaki Miyoshi

item.title: The $\mathbb{Z}/2$-equivariant Seiberg--Witten Floer cohomology of the $(2, 1)$-cable is an unknot detector
item.description: arXiv:2611.04823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a knot $K \subset S^3$ is the unknot if and only if the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-equivariant Seiberg--Witten Floer cohomology of the double cover branched along the $(2, 1)$-cable of $K$ has no $\mathbb{F}_2[Q]$-torsion. The proof combines the Thom--Gysin exact sequence, the Montesinos trick, and the genus bound for $L$-space surgeries.
item.dc:creator: Nobuo Iida, Tatsumasa Suzuki

item.title: A Wolpert Theorem for shearing coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2611.05045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A theorem from Wolpert bounds the Weil--Petersson distance from a hyperbolic surface to a maximally noded surface in terms of the lengths of the underlying pants decomposition. We prove analogues for punctured surfaces both in terms of the lambda-lengths and in terms of the shearing coordinates of an ideal triangulation.
item.dc:creator: Marie Abadie

item.title: Mapping class group actions on the cohomology of configuration spaces of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let X be a closed oriented surface of genus at least 2 and P a finite subset of X. We bound the action of the mapping class group of (X,P) on the rational cohomology groups of the ordered configuration spaces F_n(X-P) of X-P. In particular, we show that, when #P < 2, the diagonal action of the mapping class group on the direct sum of the H^n(F_n(X-P)) is faithful, and determine its kernel when #P > 1.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Dupont, Richard Hain

item.title: A Smooth Shioda-Tate Isomorphism for Elliptically Fibered 4-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.05177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a subgroup of the mapping class group of an elliptically fibered $4$-manifold $\pi: M\to B$, inspired by number theory. The smooth Mordell-Weil group $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ is the group of isotopy classes of smooth sections of $\pi$. We construct a smooth analog of the Shioda-Tate isomorphism, identifying $\mathrm{MW(\pi)}$ with the quotient of $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$ by the trivial lattice of $\pi$. This shows that $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ can be computed explicitly from $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we show that the natural inclusion of the holomorphic Mordell-Weil group into the smooth one is an isomorphism if and only if $M$ is a rational elliptic surface. As another application, we show that $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ satisfies a strong version of Nielsen realization: any torsion element of $\mathrm{MW}(\pi)$ is represented by a holomorphic translation of $M$ of the same order.
item.dc:creator: Maria Morariu

item.title: Convex ribbon disks, quasipositivity, and Lagrangian sliceness
item.description: arXiv:2611.05331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a version of convex surface theory for immersed ribbon surfaces with Legendrian boundary. As an application, we establish a special case of K3: Problem 1.70 on sharpness in the slice-Bennequin inequality implying quasipositivity, and a special case of a conjecture of Cornwell, Ng, and Sivek on characterizing Lagrangian sliceness. Specifically, we prove that if $K$ is a knot that bounds a "star-shaped" ribbon disk and satisfies $\overline{\mathrm{sl}}(K) = -1$ (resp.\ $\overline{\mathrm{tb}}(K) = -1$), then $K$ is quasipositive (resp.\ Lagrangian slice). In fact, we prove these statements for any fixed transverse (resp.\ Legendrian) representative.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Breen, Alexander Zupan

item.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
item.description: arXiv:2611.02515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincar\'e expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.
item.dc:creator: Kei Kaneda, Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: On nearly Lefschetz fibrations and spinal open books
item.description: arXiv:2611.04089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We survey the recent development of spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations. The focus is on explaining past and new results regarding the detection of symplectic fillability and classification of symplectic fillings of contact 3-manifolds in light of the new machinery. We give many examples and a list of open questions. This can be considered as an additional chapter to the lecture notes by Ozbacgi and Wendl.
item.dc:creator: Hyunki Min, Agniva Roy, Luya Wang

item.title: Finiteness properties of centralisers in $\mathrm{Out}(F_N)$ and automorphisms of free-by-cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.04581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group. We prove that the centraliser of any element of $\mathrm{Out}(F)$ or $\mathrm{Aut}(F)$ is of type $\rm{VF}$. We also prove that the (outer) automorphism group of any free-by-cyclic group $M=F\rtimes_\varphi\mathbb{Z}$ is of type $\rm{VF}$, and so are the McCool subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(M)$. This relies on the construction of a new $\mathrm{Out}(M)$-invariant splitting of $M$, that enables us to reduce the proof of the above statements to the case where the outer class of $\varphi$ has finite order.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Andrew, Yassine Guerch, Camille Horbez, Richard D. Wade

item.title: Morse accessibility with applications to Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.05332v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we begin developing a theory of Morse hierarchies for finitely generated groups. Very roughly, a Morse hierarchy is a iterative splitting of a group over subgroups that do not contribute to the Morse boundary of the ambient group. We apply this theory to Coxeter groups, establishing new combinatorial criteria that distinguish certain Coxeter groups from other Coxeter groups as well as right-angled Artin groups up to quasi-isometry. We highlight the consequences for the right-angled case. To build the reader's intuition, the last section provides many examples of Morse hierarchies and their subtleties. Finally, there is an appendix by the second author and Vivian He that extends these ideas to the metrizable Cashen--Mackay topology on the Morse boundary.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cordes, Annette Karrer, Kim Ruane

item.title: Parametrized Euler class and semicohomology theory
item.description: arXiv:2101.11971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a measurable cocycle with values in $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\mathbb{S}^1)$, we construct an $\mathrm{L}^\infty$-parametrized Euler class in bounded cohomology. We show that such a class vanishes if and only if the cocycle can be lifted to $\mathrm{Homeo}^+_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{R})$ and it admits an equivariant family of points. We recall the notion of semicohomologous cocycles and we show that two measurable cocycles are semicohomologous if and only if they induce the same parametrized Euler class. Since for minimal cocycles, semicohomology boils down to cohomology, the parametrized Euler classes of minimal cohomologous cocycles are equal. We conclude by studying the vanishing of the real parametrized Euler class and we obtain some results about elementary cocycles.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Savini

item.title: 2-Linearizability of Geometric 3-Manifold Groups Over Commutative Rings
item.description: arXiv:2608.01532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The fundamental groups of compact 3-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by only allowing finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}(2,R)$, where $R$ is a finite commutative ring. In earlier work, this conjecture was disproven in full generality. The conjecture arose in the context of orientable connected compact 3-manifolds which are geometrizable. By constructing explicit faithful linear representations using rings with nilpotent elements, we demonstrate that the conjecture holds for six of the eight Thurston model geometries, namely all but $\mathbb{S}^3$ and $\widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2}$. In the case of $\mathbb{S}^3$, the conjecture holds if we replace $\mathrm{PGL}(2,R)$ with $\mathrm{GL}(2,R)$. A spherical counterexample for the projective variant is the Poincar\'{e} homology sphere $\Sigma(2,3,5)$. In the case of $\widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2}$, the conjecture fails to hold for both the projective and non-projective variants; a counterxample is provided by the Brieskorn sphere $\Sigma(2,3,7)$.
item.dc:creator: Montek Singh Gill

item.title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
item.description: arXiv:2611.00142v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.
item.dc:creator: Montek Singh Gill

item.title: $L^2$-Betti numbers of Dehn fillings
item.description: arXiv:2412.16090v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate the study of the $L^2$-Betti numbers of group-theoretic Dehn fillings. For a broad class of virtually special groups $G$, we prove that the $L^2$-Betti numbers of sufficiently deep Dehn fillings $\overline{G}$ are equal to those of $G$. As applications, we verify the Singer Conjecture for certain Einstein manifolds, establish a virtual fibering criterion for $\overline{G}$, obtain bounds on deficiency of $\overline{G}$, and provide new examples of hyperbolic groups with exotic subgroups that arise as Dehn fillings of any cusped arithmetic hyperbolic manifold of dimension at least four.
item.dc:creator: Nansen Petrosyan, Bin Sun

item.title: Curves on the torus with few intersections
item.description: arXiv:2412.18002v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Aougab and Gaster [Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 174 (2023), 569-584] proved that any set of simple closed curves on the torus, where any two are non-homotopic and intersect at most k times, has a maximum size of $k+O(\sqrt{k}\log k)$. We determine the maximum size of such a set for every k. In particular, the maximum never exceeds k+6, and it does not exceed k+4 when k is large. As this quantity coincides with the maximal number of columns of a generic k-modular matrix with two rows, our result also settles the column number problem, a problem of interest in combinatorial optimization, for such matrices.
item.dc:creator: Igor Balla, Marek Filakovsk\'y, Bart{\l}omiej Kielak, Daniel Kr\'a\v{l}, Niklas Schlomberg

item.title: Skein and cluster algebras of punctured surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2503.15037v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the full Fock--Goncharov conjecture for the $\mathcal{A}_{SL_2,\Sigma_{g,p}}$-cluster variety associated with the moduli space of decorated twisted $SL_2$-local systems on triangulable surfaces $\Sigma_{g,p}$ with at least two punctures. Equivalently, we show that the tagged skein algebra $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$, identified with the middle cluster algebra $\mathrm{mid}(\mathcal{A})$, coincides with the upper cluster algebra $U(\Sigma)$. Inspired by the work of Shen--Sun--Weng, we introduce a localized cluster variety $\mathring{\mathcal{A}}$ whose positive real locus is the decorated Teichm\"uller space $\mathcal{T}^d(\Sigma)$. For $p\geq2$, its ring of global sections is the normalization of the classical Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ and equals that algebra except for the four-punctured sphere. In the equality cases, the quantum Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_q(\Sigma)$ provides a quantization of this global-section ring. We prove normality of $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$ for $p\geq2$, complementing its known Gorenstein property, and normality of $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$ other than $\Sigma_{0,4}$. We also prove finite generation of $U(\Sigma_{g,p})$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$, including the once-punctured case.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li
